speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: asked the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (a) whether the flood prevention systems will be able to prevent flash floods similar to those that occurred on 8 January 2018 after the completion of the drainage upgrades in 2019; (b) what are the guiding principles used to determine the drainage capacity needed in an area; and (c) whether these include balancing the potential collateral damage versus the investment cost.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: asked the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources how does PUB ensure that existing drains and canals are kept free of debris that have the potential to create constrictions or bottlenecks, so as to alleviate flooding.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: On the morning of 8 January 2018, the prevailing Northeast Monsoon, aggravated by the development of a Sumatra squall, gave rise to intense rainfall across several parts of Singapore.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This means that about half of Singapore's average monthly rainfall in January fell in just over four hours.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Eight of the nine locations that experienced flash floods that morning are low-lying and, therefore, susceptible to flash floods.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Two of these, Tampines Road, opposite Jalan Teliti, and Arumugam Road, have a history of flash floods.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The Public Utilities Board (PUB) is already carrying out drainage improvement works in these eight locations to enable the drains there to discharge more water in a shorter time when completed.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: During drainage improvement works, PUB ensures that the drainage capacity of the area is maintained at the original level before works commence.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Drainage works did not cause the flash floods in these locations.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: For the ninth location at Tampines Avenue 12, apart from intense rainfall which exceeded the drain's design capacity, a temporary construction access road built by the contractor had obstructed the earth drain in an adjacent worksite.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: PUB has worked with the developer to improve the drainage at the earth drain and this will help to improve the situation at Tampines Avenue 12 in an event of an intense storm.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The longer-term measure is the permanent drainage system which will be built in tandem with the upcoming development project at the adjacent worksite.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The flash floods were caused by the intense rainfall temporarily exceeding the existing design capacity of the drains.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Although the flood waters affected only certain stretches of the roads, and subsided within 15 to 60 minutes, we acknowledge that members of the public were inconvenienced and a number of cars were stalled.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: When flash floods occur, we urge members of the public to exercise caution and avoid traversing in submerged areas even if they appear safe.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Flash floods are usually of short duration and it is better to take a detour or wait for them to pass before continuing the journey.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: To aid the public, PUB, together with Traffic Police and the Land Transport Authority (LTA), will help divert vehicles at the earliest possible.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: PUB takes into account terrain, the extent and type of developments in the area, catchment area served by the drain, as well as the design rainfall intensity over the catchment.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: However, with climate change, we can expect more intense rainfalls to be the norm in the future.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: A study by the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research found that flood risks from rainfall changes will increase in the next two to three decades, due to global warming from greenhouse gases already emitted into the atmosphere.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The need for adaptation is significant, even in countries with good infrastructure, such as Singapore.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: To prepare for this, PUB has raised the drainage design standards since 2011, so that our drains can handle up to 45% higher rainfall intensities.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: These new standards were endorsed in 2012 by a Drainage Expert Panel comprising local and international specialists.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Since 2012, PUB has commenced and completed drainage improvement works at 327 locations.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: There are another 73 locations undergoing similar works, with 22 more planned this year.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: However, it is not feasible to build our drains to accommodate every extreme rainfall event as this would require massive land take and much higher costs.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Even with this widening, we cannot guarantee that there will be no floods in future, as rainfall events of even higher intensity could still occur that exceed the design capacity.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: To deal with the most extreme historical rainfall events, the Bedok Canal would need to be widened to at least 62 metres, displacing the Bedok Park Connector and community spaces adjacent to the canal, and possibly even affecting the surrounding residential areas.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Given competing needs for other land uses, such as housing, parks and roadsides, we have to be practical in our drainage expansion in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We have to design with practical considerations and not for extreme conditions all the time for all places.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Building our drains for extreme conditions would mean that much of the capacity would be extremely costly but not needed most of the time.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We will, however, ensure our critical infrastructure is well-protected from such extreme rainfalls.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This is achieved through the "source-pathway-receptor" approach which was developed based on the recommendation of the Drainage Expert Panel to implement a holistic range of interventions.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Under this approach, other than improving the pathways, or the drains, we also manage the source, which refers to where the rain falls.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Measures include detention tanks to slow down surface runoff and reduce the amount of storm water entering the drains during peak rainfall.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: For instance, the Stamford Detention Tank and the Stamford Diversion Canal are constructed to protect Orchard Road against floods.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Built beneath a nursery and coach bay of the Tyersall Learning Forest, the Stamford Detention Tank will temporarily hold excess storm water from the drains.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: After the rain subsides, the storm water will be pumped back into the drains for subsequent discharge into Marina Reservoir.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Apart from structural interventions, PUB places equal emphasis on non-structural measures, such as the maintenance of drains.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: PUB and the National Environment Agency's (NEA's) Department of Public Cleanliness carry out regular inspections to remove debris, litter and leaves from the drains.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We encourage everyone to keep our environment litter-free.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Any obstruction in the drain reduces its capacity and impedes water flow, which could lead to or aggravate a flash flood.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We urge developers and contractors to ensure that the drains in and around their work sites function well.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Members of the public are encouraged to provide feedback on drain conditions through PUB's MyWaters app or the Municipal Services Office's (MSO's) OneService App or call PUB's 24-hour Call Centre.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Members of the public can subscribe to NEA's and PUB's short message service (SMS) alerts or mobile apps for updates on impending heavy rain and the water level in drains at designated locations.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: While PUB strives to give early warning to the public, the weather systems in our equatorial region pose a forecasting challenge.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: During flash floods, members of the public can stay updated through radio broadcasts, PUB's Facebook and Twitter pages, mobile apps as well as LTA's Expressway Monitoring Advisory System (EMAS).

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In respect of the measures for the eight out of nine locations in the eastern part of Singapore that the Minister mentioned will be taken or undergoing, how soon will these measures be completed?

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Before I answer that question, I would like Members to recognise that PUB must also manage extremities of weather in both directions.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We have to take care of intense drought, prolonged drought, that challenges or may affect our water supply.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: At the same time, we have to take care of extreme weather, such as rain of higher intensity and frequency, which will bring about floods.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Therefore, when we talk about floods, we must also remember to ask questions about the other extreme.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: What should we do and how much resources do we have for both extremities?

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Climate change actually has brought extreme weather conditions in many parts of the world.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Many of us would have read that Paris has just experienced one of the worst floods because of the rising Seine River, prolonged rain for two weeks that recently has closed even the Louvre Museum.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: At the same time, down south, Cape Town is experiencing drought condition for three years, just like us.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: They did not put in the right things at the right time and now may run out of water within two to three months.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Cape Town is now racing to look at solutions to solve their water problem.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: If you put this end to end, from the surface of the earth, it will go through the centre of the earth with 2,000 km to spare.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: That is how long our drains, canals and rivers are.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: So, we have to be cautious about making commitments that everything will be settled quickly.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We also have to ensure that drains are not the only ones that will solve the problem.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We have to ensure at the source or the receptor of where this rainfall happens, the developers and the people who own this part of land, must also play their part.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: So, it is not easy to answer just because the drains will be ready by this time, the flash floods will be gone.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Now, together with the drain and the receptor, source and completion of all the projects there, we will have a better chance of avoiding the flash floods.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But like I said, it is impossible to totally eliminate them because this will occur.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: It is more important for us to give as much timely warning as possible to our public to ensure that they do not traverse these flash floods, which will usually go away within 50 minutes to 60 minutes.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Contractors, in preparing the site, have to submit to PUB their plans for diverting drains, for keeping the original drain design, for taking away the water from the site intact so that rainfalls or the design capacity of the drain will not affect the surrounding areas.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Where we have found flash floods occurring in areas where we know do not frequently occur or rarely occur, it is usually because the contractors have not implemented what they are supposed to do or implemented something else in order to make their worksite either accessible or easier to work on.
